mutated_regimes.reasoning: The receipt of 2,000 USDC is classified as income from the transfer of a virtual digital asset under s.115BBH. The tax rate is 30%, and no deductions or set-offs are allowed. The valuation date is the settlement date (2026-06-23) as per Rule 56, and the value is determined using the telegraphic transfer buying rate as per Rule 206. No TDS is required because the recipient is outside India, as per s.393(1) Table Sl. No. 8(vi) and the note for non-residents. Under s.439(8), a bona fide disclosure of the income with all material facts is required to avoid penalties.

uncertainty_budget.explanation: The Indian market price of the token against the official rupee rate for a dollar. This is the bulk of the gap and it is the part everyone argues about.
No rate was published on the settlement date. Stepping back to 2026-06-25 or forward to 2026-06-29 is undetermined — Rule 206 does not say which.
A daily candle is not a price. It is a range with four printed readings and no rule choosing between them.
The retrieved pair is USDT/INR. The receipt was USDC. The figure is USDT/INR x USDC/USDT, and treating the peg as exactly 1.0000 is a further choice.
